==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|æstimate}} {{qualifier|archaic}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{a|en|UK}}
** {{sense|noun}} {{IPA|en|/ˈɛs.tɪ.mət/}}
** {{sense|verb}} {{IPA|en|/ˈɛs.tɪˌmeɪt/}}
* {{a|en|US}}
** {{sense|noun}}{{IPA|en|/ˈɛs.tə.mət/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-estimate-noun.ogg|a=US}}
** {{sense|verb}} {{IPA|en|/ˈɛs.təˌmeɪt/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-estimate-verb.ogg|a=US}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|estimat}}, {{bor+|enm|la|aestimātus||valuing, estimate|pos=only used in the ablative singular: ''"aestimātū..."'' (in valuing...)|nocap=1|nocat=1}}, from {{af|la|aestimō|-tus|id2=action noun|t2=action noun-forming suffix|nocat=1}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# A rough calculation or assessment of the value, size, or cost of something.
#: {{syn|en|estimation|appraisal}}
#: {{cot|en|esteem#Noun}}
## {{lb|en|specifically|_|in|business|and|construction}} A [[document]] (or verbal notification) specifying how much a [[job]] is likely to cost.
#: {{hyper|en|quote#Noun}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1928|author=Lawrence R. Bourne
|title=Well Tackled!
|chapter=3|url=http://openlibrary.org/works/OL5387037W
|passage=“They know our boats will stand up to their work,” said Willison, “and that counts for a good deal. A low '''estimate''' from us doesn't mean scamped work, but just that we want to keep the yard busy over a slack time.”}}
# An upper limitation on some positive quantity.

===Etymology 2===
{{bor+|en|la|aestimātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|passive}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|aestimō||to estimate}} (see {{af|en|-ate|nocat=1}}), older form {{m|la|aestumō||to value, rate, esteem}}; from {{der|en|itc-ola|*ais-temos||one who cuts copper}}, meaning one in the Roman Republic who mints money. Compare {{cog|enm|estymatt|t=reputed}} / {{m|enm|estimat}}. See also the {{glossary|doublet}} {{dbt|en|esteem|notext=1}}, as well as {{m|en|aim}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# To [[calculate]] roughly, often from [[imperfect]] [[data]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2003|author=Alexander J. Field; Gregory Clark; William A. Sundstrom|title=Research in Economic History| passage=Higher real prices for durables are '''estimated''' to have reduced their consumption per capita by 1.09% in 1930, {{...}}| url=http://books.google.com/books?id=i7wBsfU878AC&lpg=PA72&dq=%22are%20estimated%20to%22&pg=PA72#v=onepage&q=%22are%20estimated%20to%22&f=false}}
# To judge and form an opinion of the value of, from imperfect data.
#* {{RQ:Locke Value|passage=It is by the weight of silver, and not the name of the piece, that men '''estimate''' commodities and exchange them.}}
